item.title: Trump hurls abuse and shows middle finger to Ford worker who shouted ‘pedophile protector’
item.description: During a Michigan visit, President Trump appeared to react angrily to a heckler shouting an insult, with video showing him gesturing with an expletive and the middle finger. This incident occurs amid ongoing scrutiny over the handling of files related to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, a figure Trump has past associations with.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘I'm alone in the dark’: Trump’s dramatic fundraising email triggers online criticism
item.description: Donald Trump is seeking donations through a fundraising email. The message warns supporters of dire consequences if he faces impeachment again. It highlights potential changes to American lives if he does not meet fundraising deadlines. The email, shared online, has drawn criticism for its tone and appeal for money.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Nick Fuentes says he wants to take over Kick and asks Adin Ross for help
item.description: Controversial online figure Nick Fuentes is reportedly seeking to dominate the streaming platform Kick, even enlisting the help of popular streamer Adin Ross. Fuentes, banned from major sites, sees Ross's influence as key to gaining a foothold and boosting his presence. The viral clip sparks debate about influencer power and Kick's future content landscape.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Executed two teenagers: Double murderer awarded £7,500 as taxpayers foot six-figure legal bill
item.description: A UK High Court ruling has awarded a convicted double murderer £7,500 in damages and £234,000 in legal costs after judges found his prison segregation breached the European Convention on Human Rights. The decision has sparked political backlash in Britain, reopening debate over extremist prisoners, taxpayer-funded payouts and whether human rights law is undermining prison security and public confidence.

item.title: Popular hunting YouTuber Ryan Lampers faces felony charges over alleged illegal kills
item.description: Montana hunting YouTuber Ryan Lampers faces serious legal trouble in Idaho, accused of unlawfully killing a mule deer, mountain lion, and wolf in 2024. Charges include shooting in restricted areas, outside hunting seasons, using wrong tags, and falsifying paperwork for reimbursement. Conviction could lead to prison time and a lifetime hunting ban.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Kai Cenat streaming retirement rumors go viral after YourRAGE’s comment
item.description: Rumors of Kai Cenat's retirement from streaming have intensified after close friend YourRAGE suggested he has already concluded his Twitch career. YourRAGE dismissed questions about Cenat's subscriber numbers, stating he is now a star pursuing movie opportunities. This follows Cenat's record-breaking Mafiathon 3 in late 2025, with no major streams since.

item.title: Scott Adams dies at 68: How 'Dilbert' cartoon strip made him famous — and what ended it
item.description: Creator of the "Dilbert" comic strip, Scott Adams, has died at 68 from aggressive prostate cancer. His passing follows the widespread discontinuation of his comic due to racist remarks made on his YouTube channel, where he suggested segregation. Newspapers cited his comments as the reason for dropping the strip.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Benevolent?’ Conservative star Nick Shirley mocked online after stumbling over word in interview - watch video
item.description: Online hero Nick Shirley, who exposed Minnesota daycare fraud, now faces mockery for not knowing the meaning of 'benevolent.' A viral video shows him mispronouncing and struggling with the word, leading to accusations of being 'stupid' and 'illiterate.' This comes after his allegations prompted federal investigations into alleged fraud.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: America in decline? Data shows even its poorest states now outperform most G7 economies
item.description: Political dysfunction and rising inequality persist, but the United States continues to anchor the global economy. Its share of world GDP has barely shifted since 1990, private wealth remains overwhelmingly concentrated, and productivity exceeds every other G7 country. Europe faces structural stagnation, while American growth is being sustained by technology, capital markets and scale.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Explained: How Elon Musk's Starlink becomes Iran protesters’ lifeline as internet blackout deepens
item.description: Iran's internet shutdowns during protests are being circumvented by SpaceX's Starlink satellite service. Despite being illegal, terminals enter the country via informal channels, offering a lifeline for communication and information sharing. Authorities attempt to jam signals and locate devices, leading to a constant technological battle, while legal risks for users escalate.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Iran unrest: Trump tells protesters ‘help is on its way’; Russia warns of ‘disastrous consequences’
item.description: Russia condemned "subversive external interference" in Iran's internal politics, warning of "disastrous consequences" after US President Donald Trump encouraged protestors. Trump's remarks followed widespread protests in Iran, triggered by economic hardship and fueled by anger over subsidy cuts and rising prices, with significant casualties reported.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk
